problem:
Evaluate
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{xy}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$

*Hint: First change the order of integration to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.$*
worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as 

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,x\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le xy}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{xy}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081417/assets/6b3720af66e81aef6792d4b2a34b2bdf2b93bd59ed6e28e4b38a1e06964bb2cc.png)

The region $D$ is type I region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,x\le y\le 1}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region $D$ is

$$
x=0
$$

and the right boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
y=x\,⟹\,x=y.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le x\le y},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081417/assets/9dc99cc0df9f089b9f62402c3c5ea9c4408be077debbf6dfadeb884ee4d8b2d0.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{xy}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}{\int }_{0}^{xy}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}[{\int }_{0}^{xy}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})\,\text{d}z]\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})[z]_{0}^{xy}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}2xy\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})[{\int }_{0}^{y}2x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})[{x}^{2}]_{0}^{y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{4})]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)-1) \\  & =\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
